_doc: Royce Pettit, the fifth gun. Sober in the Pettit back room in the mornings; on the porch swing at dusk and night once he has been calmed (the wild version is a fight on the map). Trust 1, ashamed, shaking, counts things. The red check makes him say the Lacys were shooting at him; the feed-store book is the shows table's way in.

open.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: Dessie said y'all would come. She said be civil. I'm civil mornings. Ask anybody.
I ain't got nothing for the paper. I was asleep. Everybody on this road was asleep but the Lacys and the Lord.
His hands. Look at his hands, and then don't.

passives.line: He says 'asleep' and looks at the floor between his feet, where a man looks when he's counting steps he took once.
Shotgun shells in a row on the table, red, brass up. Nine. He touches them while he talks, one, two, three, like a rosary.

options.text: We're not the paper, Mr Pettit. We don't print. We file.
You weren't asleep. Everybody on this road knows it. We'd just like to hear it from the man.
(Sit down across from him and say nothing.)

hub.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: ...All right. Ask. Low, though. She's in the kitchen.

static.line: Nine shells on the table. He fired nine. He knows which one hit something. Make him tell you which one, and what it sounded like when it hit.

options.text: You walked up a road with a gun and a pint toward a house full of children.
What do you drink to on the twenty-first, Royce? Not what. Who.
Nine shells on the table. How many did you fire that night? You know the number.

fail.line: I don't count. I just like 'em in a row. Dessie says I'm particular.

options.text: Cleve Hardin heard a gun walking the road. The Lacys were firing back. Say the part you've never said, Royce. They were shooting at you.
The gun's on the swing with the action open and the shells in a row. You put it there yourself.
That's all for now, Mr Pettit.

hard.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: I thought they needed help. That's the God's truth and it's no excuse.
I heard shooting and I thought, Royce, go help, and I took Daddy's gun and the rest of the pint and I went.
There was eleven people in that house and three of 'em under ten and I put shot in the fence forty feet from the porch. You can say it.

who.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: She came across the road in '56 with a pie. A pie. Set it on this table and said, Royce, we're all right, and went home.
Never said another word about it, not in twenty years.
She knew. She'd have been at the window. She knew whose shirt that was in the tobacco and she brought me a pie. I drink to her.
A pie's a slap, honey. From a woman like that, a pie is the hardest thing she could have carried over.

who_no.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: I drink to the twenty-first. That's who.
Go ask Brother Tilley what I drink to, he's had it off me every August and he ain't told nobody yet.

count.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: Box of fours holds twenty-five and Daddy'd used some, and I come home with eleven.
I've had nine on this table since 1955 and never bought another.
Two at the house. God forgive me. Five walking, at the eyes. Two straight up under the oak, 'cause by then the eyes was over my head.
The eyes didn't go out. Nine shots and the eyes didn't go out. You tell me what it was, you're the ones with the file.
Eyes over his head under the gully oak. Two shots of birdshot into a roost.
Every owl in that tree came down on him and he saw it as the eyes not going out.

shot_at.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: Something hit the mailbox beside my head like a handful of gravel. Then the fence post.
I was in the tobacco with my face in the dirt and the shot was going through the leaves over me like rain.
They was shooting at the thing on the fence. The thing on the fence was me, with Daddy's gun, drunk.
And then it wasn't me, 'cause I'd crawled, and they kept shooting. So I don't know. I don't know what it was after I crawled.
I been not knowing in this chair thirty-nine years. That's the whole thing. That's all of it.
That's as honest as a witness gets. He was the thing on the fence, and then he wasn't, and the shooting went on. Both halves are true.

shot_at_no.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: Cleve Hardin. Cleve Hardin never said a word to me in thirty-nine years and he said it to you.
Get out of my sister's house. Come back when you ain't carrying Cleve Hardin in your mouth.

feed_book.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: ...That's me. 'A neighbour of theirs, on his way home from town.' That's Stokes's granddaddy's writing. 'Already had some.'
He meant whiskey. He sold me the double-ought anyhow.
Then I went by Oates' for the fours and the pint, 'cause I didn't have enough of either. That's a man getting ready.
Two stores sold me shells that day and neither one asked what for. Nobody on this road ever asked me what for.
Two shell books, two stores, one afternoon. That's not a man who heard shooting and ran to help. That's a man who was going anyway.

porch.speaker: kc_drunk
lines: ...I did. First time it's been out of my hands on the twenty-first since 1955.
Thirty-nine Augusts I sat here with it across my knees waiting on them to come back. They never did. Y'all did. I about shot West Virginia.
Leave it there. Dessie can see it from the door. She ain't seen it with the action open in her life, and I'd like her to look a while.
He's not guarding the road any more. He's letting her watch him not guard it. That's the night ending, thirty-nine years late.
